summary:
Turn 90 recorded a construction obstacle honestly rather than producing a weaker witness.

What was attempted. I set out to extend the confirmed owner-alive re-proposal protection (C5) to the client's actual reply: commit the re-proposed instance, execute it, and observe bytes written to the client's writer. The attempt showed that the harness which drives that scenario is the simpler one and has no peer-message delivery helper, so the re-proposed instance's PreAccept reply would have to be prepared by hand instead of being produced by a peer's handler — exactly the substitution the protocol findings have been careful to avoid. I stopped rather than file a check whose witness rests on a prepared reply.

What is recorded instead. The mechanism stays confirmed and unchanged: the operation is put back on the propose channel (C5's artifact, reviewed), and the reply path is unchanged — execution applies the committed commands and answers the client while the proposal is still attached. The missing piece is only an end-to-end observation, and the note says precisely what it needs: a harness that both drives the re-proposal and delivers peer messages through the real codec, which is machinery the recovery harnesses already have and could be combined. The note also keeps the other residuals visible: the reader-side reaction to a displaced stream (not exercisable in-package), the two paused candidates' resume conditions, the attribution issue on the superseded C1 artifact, and the interpretation question for the inert transitive-conflict branch.

State. Audit spec version 20; the twelve claim families and their reviewed artifacts are untouched, the map is current at version 19, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened. The audit's outstanding work is now a short, explicit list rather than an open-ended frontier.
